title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Forestry (2015)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Forestry (2015). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: The most important of timber harvest planning is to:
questions.explanation: Estimating harvest production is crucial for effective timber harvest planning as it enables proper resource allocation, equipment scheduling, and financial forecasting for the forestry operation.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not the importance of harvesting tree:
options: Improving the health of the forest
Controlling the types of trees that grow on the site
Producing paper, lumber and numerous forest products
questions.explanation: Destroying certain wildlife species is not an importance of harvesting trees.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not the result of having Knowledge on biology of a given Non-timber forest product:
questions.explanation: All listed options are results of having knowledge on biology of non-timber forest products.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not the element of non-timber forest product in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: Timber is not considered a non-timber forest product.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statement is correct?
options: If the buttress height is less than one meter then DBH measurement is taken at the point where buttress ends
If a tree bifurcates above breast height then DBH measurement is taken separately on each stem
For trees on slope, DBH measurement is taken at the standard height above the floor/ground on the lowhill side of the tree.
For leaning tree, DBH measurement is carried out at parallel to the lean on the upper side of the lean
questions.explanation: DBH measurement for bifurcating trees is taken separately on each stem.

questions.questionText: A function of taxonomy, which deals with the determination of correct names of a plants is referred to as:
questions.explanation: Nomenclature is the function of taxonomy that deals with naming plants.

questions.questionText: The changes in forest stand structure with time, including stand behavior after disturbances is known as:
questions.explanation: Stand dynamics refers to changes in forest stand structure over time.

questions.questionText: The two major techniques of seed collection are:
options: Collection seeds/fruits from the ground and from the crown
Collection from natural tree and crown
questions.explanation: The two major techniques are collecting seeds from the ground and from the crown.

questions.questionText: The minimum area required for forest is _____hectare?
questions.explanation: The minimum area required for a forest is 1 hectare.

questions.questionText: The total amount of water found in seeds, usually expressed as percentage.
questions.explanation: Moisture content refers to the total amount of water found in seeds.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not the aim of herbarium:
options: Preserve the catalogues of seeds and dried herbarium plants
questions.explanation: Plant pressing and drying is not the primary aim of a herbarium.

questions.questionText: The art, science and practice of controlling the establishment, composition, health, quality and growth of the vegetation of forest stands is known as:
questions.explanation: Silviculture is the practice of managing forest stands.

questions.questionText: Complete forest inventory explains:
options: Forest measurement made in some sample plot
Inventory carried out on the entire forest
Survey of forest resource takes place on systematically selected plots of the forest area
Inventory taken from small part of the forest
questions.explanation: Complete forest inventory involves measuring the entire forest.

questions.questionText: Which practice comprises under the silvi pastoral system?
questions.explanation: Protein banks are a silvopastoral practice where leguminous fodder trees and shrubs are grown in blocks to provide high-protein feed for livestock. The Taungya system is an agrisilvicultural practice, not silvopastoral.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following causes of raising fire in natural forests?
questions.explanation: Human activities are a common cause of forest fires.

questions.questionText: All are correct suggestions about definitions of agroforestry except one:
options: An agroforestry system always has two or more outputs
The cycle of an AF system is always more than a year
Even the simplest AF system is more complex
Potential trees to serve as hosts of insect pests that are harmful to food crops
questions.explanation: Potential trees serving as hosts for pests is not a definition of agroforestry.

questions.questionText: What are the disadvantages of clear cutting methods for regeneration?
options: Vigorous growth of grasses and weeds and encourage soil erosion
Make most of the wild animal's home less
questions.explanation: Clear cutting can lead to soil erosion and uncontrolled growth of weeds.

questions.questionText: The forest valuation approach which provides an indication of value by converting future cash flows to a single current capital value is?
questions.explanation: The income approach converts future cash flows to present value.

questions.questionText: Which one is not most commonly asked the questions in a conflict assessment?
options: Who are the significantly affected stakeholders?
questions.explanation: The statement 'What I know is enough' is not a question in conflict assessment.

questions.questionText: Seed maturity judged by field methods in:
options: Determining the maximum dry weight of seeds
questions.explanation: Field methods for seed maturity include color and cutting tests.

questions.questionText: __________ refers to the environmental condition and ecological suitability of systems based on the assumption that certain types of systems can be more appropriate for certain ecological conditions.
questions.explanation: Ecological basis refers to the suitability of systems for specific environmental conditions.

questions.questionText: A sample that is a small quantity of seed taken out from a single position in the seed lot:
questions.explanation: A primary sample is taken from a single position in the seed lot.

questions.questionText: From the economic classifications of the tree which one of following characteristics is categorized under silviculturally non-desirable trees?
questions.explanation: Weed trees are considered silviculturally non-desirable due to their harmful effects.

questions.questionText: ____________ are those individuals or groups who are directly involved in the conflict, or who may be affected by how the conflict is resolved.
questions.explanation: Stakeholders are directly involved or affected by the conflict.

questions.questionText: Which one is the importance of mulching?
options: Reduce the effects of insects and pests
questions.explanation: Mulching has multiple benefits including reducing evaporation and improving fertility.

questions.questionText: ______ is the average height of 100 thickest trees per hectare.
questions.explanation: Dominant height is the average height of the thickest trees in a hectare.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following Ethiopian regional states is the richest by hosting all genuses of gum and resin bearing species?
questions.explanation: Afar is known for hosting all genera of gum and resin-bearing species.

questions.questionText: The tradable forest product which is created by peeling the bark from the tree, drying most of the water out of the wood, and then treating it with a chemical to fight off insects and decay is:
questions.explanation: Poles are treated wood products created by debarking, drying, and chemically treating logs to prevent insect damage and decay, making them suitable for utility poles, fence posts, and construction supports.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following comprising under nature of components in agroforestry system?
questions.explanation: Agrisilviculture is a component of agroforestry systems.

questions.questionText: The preconditions of natural forest regeneration dynamics depend upon:
options: Sufficient volume of viable seeds, appropriate climatic and edaphic conditions
questions.explanation: Natural forest regeneration dynamics depend on viable seeds and suitable conditions.

questions.questionText: Factors not affecting the viability of stored seeds are:
questions.explanation: The word 'seed' itself is not a factor affecting seed viability. The key factors affecting stored seed viability include storage conditions, moisture content, temperature, maturity at collection, and genetic factors.

questions.questionText: The simplest and most desirable form of forest accounting is?
questions.explanation: The tree farm journal is a simple form of forest accounting.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not the primary function of Sustainable forest management?
options: Provides optimum forest products and services
Enhances environmental and economic values of forests
questions.explanation: Sustainable forest management aims to maintain employment and revenue, not decrease it.

questions.questionText: One of the following is the correct order of PFM process:
questions.explanation: The correct order of the Participatory Forest Management process is Investigation, Negotiation, Implementation.

questions.questionText: Seed maturity judged by laboratory methods except:
questions.explanation: Color is not a laboratory method for judging seed maturity.

questions.questionText: Which one is not a required parameter to define forest?
questions.explanation: Altitude is not a required parameter to define a forest. The standard parameters typically include minimum area, tree height, and crown cover percentage.

questions.questionText: Factors not affecting the viability of stored seeds are:
questions.explanation: The term 'seed' itself is not a factor affecting seed viability. Key factors include storage conditions, moisture content, temperature, seed health, and genetic characteristics.

questions.questionText: Seeds that can be dried to moisture content of approximately 5% and can be stored at a low or freezing temperature (-18oC) for a long time.
questions.explanation: Orthodox seeds can be stored at low moisture content for extended periods.

questions.questionText: How many methods are there to harvest timber?
questions.explanation: There are generally three methods to harvest timber.

questions.questionText: Which one is incorrect about spacing in plantation?
options: Wide spacing increases the cost of production
Wide spacing required for large crown species
questions.explanation: Wide spacing typically decreases the cost of production as it requires fewer seedlings, less planting labor, and reduces the need for early thinning operations. However, it may underutilize site potential.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following plants press steps is correct?
options: Plywood press - Blotter - Corrugate - 10 sheets of torn newspaper with specimen - Blotter - Corrugate - Plywood press
Plywood press - Corrugate - Blotter - 10 sheets of torn newspaper with specimen - Blotter - Corrugate - Plywood press
Plywood press - 10 sheets of torn newspaper with specimen - Corrugate - Blotter - Blotter - Corrugate - Plywood press
Plywood press - Corrugate - Blotter - Corrugate - 10 sheets of torn newspaper with specimen - Blotter - Plywood press
questions.explanation: The correct pressing steps involve using corrugate and blotters in the specified order.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is agroforestry productivity evaluation approach?
questions.explanation: Land equivalent ratio (LER) is a method for evaluating agroforestry productivity.

questions.questionText: Among listed alternatives one is instruments used for height measurement:
questions.explanation: Haga altimeter is an instrument used for measuring height.

questions.questionText: Which type of spacing provides more uniform tree crown development?
questions.explanation: Square spacing allows for more uniform tree crown development.

questions.questionText: A preservation or improvement and control of damage to forest from natural or man-made causes is known as:
questions.explanation: Forest protection involves preserving and improving forests from various damages.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not the activity of NTFP value chain?
questions.explanation: All listed options are activities in the NTFP value chain.

questions.questionText: A collection of pressed and dried plants arranged in some order and available for reference or study is known as:
questions.explanation: A herbarium is a collection of pressed and dried plants.

questions.questionText: From the following pollutants, which could highly affect aquatic ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Organic pollutants can severely impact aquatic ecosystems.

questions.questionText: __ is the emergence and development of the seedling to a stage where the aspect of its essential structures indicate whether or not it is able to develop further into a satisfactory plant under normal conditions in the soil.
questions.explanation: Germination refers to the development of a seedling into a plant.

questions.questionText: Which one of following are adverse effects of tree in agroforestry system?
options: Nutrient competition between trees and crops
Moisture competition between trees and crops
Production of substances which inhibit germination or growth
Modification of extremes of soil temperature
questions.explanation: Trees can compete with crops for nutrients in agroforestry systems.

questions.questionText: What are the principles of silviculture in forest managements?
options: To produce high-quality timber and knot-free trees
To transport the forest products to customers
questions.explanation: The primary principle of silviculture is to produce high-quality timber.

questions.questionText: A typical forest property description might include the following, except one, which one is it?
options: An aerial photo of the property
questions.explanation: The answer is 'None of the above' because all listed items (aerial photo, tax ID number, and assessed value) are typically included in a forest property description.

questions.questionText: One of the following is incorrect about the role of participatory forest management:
options: Increase awareness creation toward forest management
questions.explanation: Participatory forest management aims to reduce conflict among communities.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following site is categorized under moderately stony?
questions.explanation: 15 – 30% stoniness is categorized as moderately stony.

questions.questionText: Which one reveals how humans use models from the natural world to solve problems in agriculture, medicine, manufacturing, and commerce?
questions.explanation: Biomimicry involves using natural models to solve human problems.

questions.questionText: The types of firefighting in the forest is done by carrying out the activities of:
questions.explanation: Firefighting involves using water, soil, and chemicals.

questions.questionText: The ultimate aim of forest inventory should be:
options: Providing information on the quality and quantity of stock available
Provide the basis for sound forest management
Protecting and reasonable utilization of existing resources
Describe the past time deforestation rate alone
questions.explanation: The ultimate aim of forest inventory is to provide a basis for sound management.

questions.questionText: Improper tree felling operations may result in:
options: Improving value of the stand remaining after the cutting
questions.explanation: Improper felling can lead to high cutting costs.

questions.questionText: From the following, one is not the function of herbarium:
options: Serves as an aid in teaching botany
It serves as a source for collections biodiversity
Serves as a fundamental resource for identification of all plants of the world
questions.explanation: Studying plant anatomy is not a primary function of a herbarium.

questions.questionText: If the square spacing (2 m x 2 m) is used for plantation, how many seedlings could be planted per hectare?
questions.explanation: In square spacing of 2m x 2m, 2500 seedlings can be planted per hectare.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following promotes sustainable forest management in our country through community participation?
questions.explanation: Participatory Forest Management (PFM) promotes sustainable management through community involvement.

questions.questionText: What are the disadvantages of using insecticides?
options: Provide effective means of modifying population size of pest insects
Provide dramatic effects on pest populations within a short period of time
Damage on non-target organisms present in the environment
Some of them have broad spectrum effect while others have narrow spectrum effects
questions.explanation: Insecticides can harm non-target organisms in the environment.

questions.questionText: The fire behavior is determined except:
questions.explanation: Wood species does not directly determine fire behavior.

questions.questionText: Which method of harvesting trees is the most economical?
questions.explanation: Clear cutting is often the most economical method of harvesting.

questions.questionText: Recalcitrant seeds: This cannot survive being dried below relatively high moisture content (often 20 - 25%) and may store for a short period of time.
questions.explanation: Recalcitrant seeds cannot be dried below a certain moisture content.

questions.questionText: Integrated pest management is a philosophy, concept and methodology for dealing with:
options: Destructive disease and insect species in forests
Selecting good species for lumber productions
Chemicals which are used for killing insects
questions.explanation: Integrated pest management focuses on managing pests and diseases in forests.

questions.questionText: Before a planned felling operation what is the detailed information to collect on timber stock during silvicultural operations?
options: The societies depending on the forests
Deciding which trees should be retained after felling and commercial species
Types of animals used forests as their home
questions.explanation: Information on which trees to retain is crucial before felling.

questions.questionText: Which is not required for germination?
questions.explanation: Soil is not strictly required for germination. Seeds can germinate in various media or even without any medium (hydroponics) as long as they have adequate moisture, oxygen, and appropriate temperature.

questions.questionText: During silvicultural operations of the natural forest how to solve conflicts between societies and timber harvesting organizations?
options: Openly discussion and decided on mutual benefits
Government by its authority used all benefits
questions.explanation: Open discussions can help resolve conflicts between stakeholders.

questions.questionText: From the stand dynamics which one of the following is categorized under the characteristics of mature or optimal phase?
options: Natural succession of forests beginning on a large
Regenerative patterns and growth cycles of many tree species
Horizontal expansion of the crown and diameter growth and co-dominant or dominant should be occurred
questions.explanation: Mature or optimal phase is characterized by horizontal crown expansion and growth.

questions.questionText: Refers to regeneration obtained from vegetative parts of tree:
questions.explanation: Coppice forest refers to regeneration from vegetative parts.

questions.questionText: The forest management certification which enables consumers to identify and choose products that support responsible forest management?
questions.explanation: Chain of custody certification helps consumers identify responsibly managed forest products.

questions.questionText: What is not the basic attributes of forest ecosystem management?
options: The dynamic character of forest ecosystem management
questions.explanation: Habitat loss is not an attribute of forest ecosystem management.

questions.questionText: Information forest inventory obtained through field data surveying is called:
questions.explanation: Ground survey refers to information obtained through field data surveying.

questions.questionText: ____________ is the practice of applying a protective layer usually dead vegetative materials.
questions.explanation: Mulching involves applying a protective layer of dead vegetative materials.

questions.questionText: Commonly grows more rapidly than embryo during the period immediately after fertilization. It accumulates reserved foods: it is rich in carbohydrates, fats, proteins & growth hormones.
questions.explanation: Endosperm is the part of the seed that provides nutrition to the developing embryo.

questions.questionText: Why open areas should have first priority for planting?
options: Clearing and cultivation need too much cost
questions.explanation: Open areas are often more susceptible to erosion, making them a priority for planting.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the factors affecting the growth of natural forest during conversion systems?
options: The presence of wild animals in the forests
The presence of wild animals in the forests
questions.explanation: Edaphic conditions are critical factors affecting forest growth.

questions.questionText: All are the main aim of rehabilitation except:
options: It is important for many species to be able to migrate over great distances
To ensure the long-term stability of habitats required for the site
To establish and sustain natural ecosystems that align with the agreed future land use.
Partially or fully repair the capacity of ecosystems to provide habitats for biota and services for people.
questions.explanation: While migration is important, it is not a primary aim of rehabilitation.

questions.questionText: Why developing, evaluating and implementing prescriptions is the central activity of applied professional forestry in forest management plan?
options: Because it sets a schedule of silvicultural activities for forest management
Because it unguided the development of management proposal and its implementation
Because it directs the applied mensuration techniques during forest management
Because it guides the incurred cost and final benefit of the investment
questions.explanation: Setting a schedule for silvicultural activities is central to effective forest management.

questions.questionText: The seeds that are kept under conditions that maintain viability at reduced physiological activity, and protecting seeds from deterioration and desiccation by fungi and insect attack.
questions.explanation: Viability refers to the ability of seeds to remain viable under specific conditions.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about harvesting?
options: Treatment of dead or damaged trees in the area
It is the total process of cutting down trees and delivering them to a mill
Pruning the branches of tree at the stand
questions.explanation: Harvesting encompasses the entire process of cutting and delivering trees.

questions.questionText: Which is not correct about planting operation?
options: Seedlings should be transported under adequate shading
The seedlings should be well watered for two days before being transported to the plantation site.
The seedlings should be planted within 96 hours of extraction from nursery.
Planting should be done immediately after seedlings are distributed to the planting site.
questions.explanation: The statement that seedlings should be planted within 96 hours is incorrect. Best practices recommend planting seedlings within 24-48 hours of extraction from the nursery to ensure maximum survival and establishment.

questions.questionText: Which one is not correct about survival count and enrichment planting?
options: Survival count can be done already 2 - 3 weeks after planting
When survival is less than 80% but more than 25% beat in - up is carried out.
If survival is less than 25% the plantation needs enrichment planting
Beating – up is not usually done when survival rate is over 80% unless there are large patches with many failures.
questions.explanation: It is incorrect that survival count can be done 2-3 weeks after planting. The first survival assessment should typically be conducted 3-6 months after planting to allow seedlings time to establish and to account for delayed mortality.

questions.questionText: The process by which a specimen is attached to a sheet of mounting paper and a label affixed at the lower right corners referred to as:
questions.explanation: Mounting refers to the process of attaching specimens to sheets.

questions.questionText: If the rectangle spacing (2 m x 1 m) is used for plantation, how many seedlings could be planted per hectare?
questions.explanation: In rectangular spacing of 2m x 1m, 5000 seedlings can be planted per hectare.

questions.questionText: Which one are not the correct procedures that should be followed for any planting?
options: Firm the soil around the roots by stamping/healing
On dry sites planting positions must maximize water retention
questions.explanation: Using plastic containers is not a standard procedure for planting.

questions.questionText: The removal of fruit or seeds with impurities like small parts of fruit, leaves, twigs, empty seeds, foreign seeds, and chaffs or totally your seeds should be clean from any other seeds/fruit parts is:
questions.explanation: Pre-cleaning is the process of removing impurities from seeds.

questions.questionText: Which one is/are the pre-conditions for Participatory Forest Management to be conducted by the central government?
questions.explanation: Decentralization is a pre-condition for effective Participatory Forest Management.

questions.questionText: Which is not the phenomenon rapidly declining largely populations of wildlife?
questions.explanation: Legal wildlife trade is not a primary cause of rapid population decline.

questions.questionText: __ is a type of forest established by through natural regeneration.
questions.explanation: Natural forest is established through natural regeneration processes.

questions.questionText: ____________ provides uniform space for expansion of the tree crown but precisely not uniform.
questions.explanation: Rectangular spacing allows for uniform crown expansion while not being perfectly uniform.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is/are indirect drivers of deforestation?
questions.explanation: All listed options are considered indirect drivers of deforestation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is considered as current asset in forest business management?
questions.explanation: Cash on hand is classified as a current asset in business management.

questions.questionText: Which one has good self-pruning species?
questions.explanation: Cuppressus lustanica is known for its good self-pruning characteristics.

questions.questionText: To modify or regulate pest population the delivery systems of insecticides are determined except?
options: The type of forest situation to be treated
The natural history of the specific target insect
The formulation requirements for the approved insecticide
questions.explanation: The number of insects alone doesn't determine the delivery system of insecticides. The critical factors are the forest situation, target insect behavior and lifecycle, and insecticide formulation requirements. Insecticide application methods are based on pest biology rather than simply their quantity.

questions.questionText: Which soil pH is categorized under acid?
questions.explanation: Soil pH less than 4.5 is categorized as acidic.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the type of fire protection from the forests accepts?
questions.explanation: Removing fuel is a common method of fire protection in forests.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true about Forest Management Agreement?
options: It clearly details the negotiated and agreed rights and responsibilities of both parties
It clearly details the negotiated and agreed rights and responsibilities of one party
It does not negotiate and agree on rules and regulations for the sustainable management of the forest resources.
It does not legally binding contract between community-based institution and the government.
questions.explanation: A Forest Management Agreement outlines the rights and responsibilities of both parties.

questions.questionText: Which one is the agricultural practices cause for land degradation?
questions.explanation: Poor tillage practices are a significant cause of land degradation.
